meta.fieldNote: The 2026 CrossFit Games individual field is set: 30 men and 30 women. 23 per division qualified at the in-person licensed Semifinals (plus the NorCal Classic), and the final 7 per division came through the online Individual Semifinal (June 11-15). Online Semifinal results are unofficial pending CrossFit video review (finalized June 29).

interviewSeries.series: Dave Castro 2026 CrossFit Games athlete interviews

men.name: James Sprague
men.storyline: The 2024 Fittest Man on Earth, who won the title in just his second individual season before finishing a razor-thin 3rd in 2025, qualified second behind Pepper at the Legends Championship. The 22-year-old former champion runs his own Next Gen Performance and is determined to reclaim the throne in San Jose.

men.name: Jayson Hopper
men.storyline: The reigning Fittest Man on Earth (2025 champion, edging Ricky Garard by 14 points) has no automatic bye, so the ex-Clemson wide receiver had to re-qualify the hard way. After a groin injury scratched him from the Mayhem Classic, he chose the French Throwdown and dominated it by 87 points, never finishing outside the top nine, signaling the champ is fit and ready to defend.

men.name: Jeffrey Adler
men.storyline: Canada's 2023 Fittest on Earth and back-to-back Rogue Invitational champion (2024, 2025) booked his spot in third at the Mayhem Classic. After a steady 8th in 2025, the Montreal gym owner remains the country's biggest podium hope and a proven champion who can win on any given day.

men.name: Jay Crouch
men.storyline: A longtime fixture of the Australian scene who broke through to a stunning 6th-place individual debut at the 2025 Games, Crouch backed it up by topping the 2026 Quarterfinals worldwide and finishing 2nd at the Torian Pro. He even ran a fundraiser to cover travel to San Jose, where he aims to prove the breakout was no fluke.

men.name: Saxon Panchik
men.storyline: One of the three competing Panchik brothers, Saxon returns to the individual Games stage as the 2026 Syndicate Crown champion, beating a stacked North American field that included rising star Ty Jenkins. A perennial top-10 threat seeking to push back toward the podium peak of his 2021 5th-place run.

men.name: Dallin Pepper
men.storyline: The three-time teen world champion (2017-2019) who exploded onto the elite scene with a runner-up finish in 2024 dominated the 2026 Legends Championship to qualify first. At 24 with elite engine and barbell strength, Pepper is squarely in the conversation to chase his first individual Games title.

men.name: Victor Hoffer
men.storyline: A former gymnast turned breakout French star, Hoffer won the 2026 Mayhem Classic semifinal outright (beating Khrennikov on a tiebreak) and arrives healthy after a heartbreaking 2024 Games rookie debut he had to abandon with a knee injury. Watch whether the 22-year-old can finally show his full ceiling on the Games floor in San Jose.

men.name: Ben Fowler
men.storyline: A New Zealand national champion, coach and programmer out of CrossFit Selwyn who previously reached the Games only as part of a team (2022). For his individual breakthrough he flew to South Africa and blew open the REBEL Renegade Games, winning by over 100 points to become the Fittest from that Semifinal and earn his first solo Games berth.

men.name: Moritz Fiebig
men.affiliate: CrossFit Sankt Pauli / Sankt Pauli Athletik
men.storyline: The Hamburg gym owner and former bodybuilder who became 'a German kid' hanging with the world's best returns for a fifth straight Games run after a career-best 19th in 2025. He edged countryman-rival pack and Nika Maisuradze by a single point for 2nd at a stacked French Throwdown, showing the consistency that has made him a fixture of the European scene.

men.name: Aniol Ekai
men.storyline: Spain's standout has carried the best Games finish in Spanish history (18th in his 2024 debut) and answered it by winning the MAD Fitness Festival outright, never finishing below 9th across six events. He returns to San Jose as the clear leader of Spain's deepest-ever Games contingent and a quietly dangerous all-rounder.

men.name: Tudor Magda
men.storyline: A former teen Games champion (Boys 14-15 in 2018) of Romanian-American heritage who broke into the top 10 as an individual in 2025, Magda dominated the NorCal Classic with 596 points, winning two events and never placing worse than 12th. At 23 he is one of the brightest young American hopes chasing a podium.

men.name: Ricky Garard
men.storyline: The redemption arc continues: stripped of his 2017 third-place podium for a failed drug test and banned four years, Garard returned clean and climbed to runner-up at the 2025 Games. After winning the 2026 Oceania Semifinal he is openly chasing his first Games title in San Jose, saying 'the job's not done yet.'

men.name: Nika Maisuradze
men.storyline: A former American-football running back and MVP of Georgia's Rustavi Steelers, the Tbilisi athlete grabbed the third and final French Throwdown ticket by just one point over Moritz Fiebig. His clutch podium finish makes him the first individual men's Games qualifier from Georgia and a breakout rookie story for the region.

men.name: Austin Hatfield
men.storyline: From training solo in West Virginia (and running a rabbit farm) to a 10th-place rookie year in 2024 and a breakout 5th at the 2025 Games, Hatfield won the 2026 Quarterfinals worldwide (beating Jeffrey Adler by 20 points) before squeaking onto the Games via 3rd at Syndicate Crown. A Mayhem-backed dark horse trending upward fast.

men.name: Bayley Martin
men.storyline: The Rotorua veteran suffered a mini heart attack at the 2025 Torian Pro that forced his withdrawal, but he recovered, won the Down Under Championship on return, and grabbed the final Oceania Games ticket in 2026. His comeback from a cardiac scare to the Games floor is one of the season's most resilient stories.

men.name: Dylan Hamming
men.storyline: A multi-time team Games competitor (5th with 8th Day CrossFit in 2024) finally making the leap to the individual field, Hamming overcame a rough 24th in one NorCal event to take 2nd overall and his first individual Games berth. After narrowly missing at the Legends Championship (3rd), the NorCal runner-up finish is the validating breakthrough of a long grind.

men.name: Henrik Haapalainen
men.storyline: After missing the 2025 Games, the Finnish veteran (a former skateboarder turned five-time Games qualifier) engineered a comeback by traveling to the Far East Throwdown in Busan and winning it outright, sealed when Sven Geens missed a final hang power clean. His return to the individual field is a redemption arc for one of Europe's most experienced competitors.

men.name: Roman Khrennikov
men.semifinalFinish2026: 2nd (525 pts, tied on points, lost tiebreak to Hoffer)
men.storyline: The perennial podium threat who overcame years of visa struggles to compete in the US now trains out of CrossFit Mayhem in Tennessee, where he qualified by tying Hoffer on points at the Mayhem Classic. After back-to-back 9th-place Games finishes, the Russian strongman is hunting a return to the podium he reached in 2022.

men.name: Calum Clements
men.storyline: The British-rooted, Spain-representing breakout of recent Spanish CrossFit (20th in 2024, 16th in 2025) grabbed the third MAD ticket with a dramatic finish, banking a perfect 200 points across the final two events to edge Jonne Koski by two. A gym co-founder who trains eight hours a day, he is on a clear upward trajectory.

men.name: Kalyan Souza
men.storyline: South America's steadily rising standout claimed his biggest win yet by taking the 2026 Copa Sur semifinal in a dramatic final-event swing, edging Chile's Benjamin Reyes. A Games veteran since 2023 who has climbed the rankings each year, the Brazilian (now based in the UAE at CrossFit Al Ain) is the continent's flag-bearer in San Jose.

men.name: Benjamin Reyes
men.storyline: One of the first two rookies to punch a ticket to the 2026 Games, the 21-year-old Chilean finished a razor-thin 2nd at Copa Sur, just 4 points behind winner Kalyan Souza. A former age-group competitor (10th in Boys 16-17 in 2022), he now arrives in San Jose as a fresh face from South America to watch in his individual debut.

men.name: Luis Cuellar
men.storyline: A former competitive skier who only turned to CrossFit in 2020, the Granada native punched his first Games ticket with a model of consistency at MAD, taking 2nd without winning a single event on the back of six top-10 finishes. A strength-and-weightlifting specialist, he is one of three Spaniards making this a breakout year for the country.

men.name: Ty Jenkins
men.storyline: The teen prodigy who won three straight CrossFit Games teen titles (2021-2023) and made his individual debut in 2025, Jenkins is back at just 19 after taking 2nd at the 2026 Syndicate Crown (tied on points with Hatfield, winning the tiebreak on event wins). The sport's brightest young talent looking to crack the elite top tier.

men.name: Guilherme Malheiros
men.storyline: Brazil's Gui Malheiros, a former teen Games champion out of Macae, trains on the Mayhem program and owns a career-best 7th at the 2021 Games. After a quiet 2024 (35th), he reset and won the 2026 online Individual Semifinal outright to book his return to San Jose.

men.name: Quinn Robinson
men.storyline: An individual rookie who has reached the Games only on a team before (12th in 2024), Robinson trains at CrossFit Trivium near Nashville. After leading early at the Syndicate Crown and just missing, he took the online route and finished 2nd in the 2026 Individual Semifinal as the only rookie in a qualifying spot.

men.name: Nick Mathew
men.storyline: The head coach at CrossFit Tonka in Minnetonka, Minnesota, Mathew was the 2022 Games Rookie of the Year (14th) and has added two more individual trips since. He finished 3rd in the 2026 online Individual Semifinal to lock in his fourth Games appearance.

men.name: Justin Medeiros
men.storyline: The two-time Fittest Man on Earth (2021 and 2022 champion) from Lodi, California now trains in Vancouver, Washington. After withdrawing from the Legends Championship, Medeiros took the online route and finished 4th in the 2026 Individual Semifinal, returning to chase a third title in San Jose.

men.name: Spencer Panchik
men.storyline: The youngest of the competing Panchik brothers, Spencer trains out of his brother Scott's CrossFit Mentality affiliate in Mentor, Ohio. A two-time individual Games athlete (20th in 2022, 17th in 2023), he booked his 2026 return by placing 5th in the online Individual Semifinal after missing the in-person qualifying spots.

men.name: Colten Mertens
men.storyline: An Iowa hog farmer who lifts before sunrise on the family farm, Mertens is a four-time individual Games athlete who climbed to 12th in 2025 and won the 2026 worldwide CrossFit Open. Strength is his calling card despite his shorter frame. He punched his ticket with a 6th-place finish in the online Individual Semifinal.

men.name: Patrick Vellner
men.storyline: One of the most decorated men in the sport, the chiropractor from Red Deer, Alberta has stood on the Games podium five times, including three runner-up finishes. Now 36 and in what he has called his final season, he secured his 2026 berth with a 7th-place finish in the online Individual Semifinal, one more shot at the title that has eluded him.

women.name: Lucy Campbell
women.storyline: The 2025 Games runner-up and reigning 2026 worldwide Open champion, Campbell qualified via the Mayhem Classic (3rd). A former international swimmer and the second British woman to reach the Games as an individual, she enters 2026 as a genuine title threat after her breakthrough silver-medal season.

women.name: Mirjam von Rohr
women.storyline: A back-to-back worldwide CrossFit Open champion (2024, 2025) and the current iF3 World Champion, von Rohr stunned the field with a 7th-place finish as a rookie at the 2025 Games, including winning the 1RM Back Squat event. In 2026 she won Open workout 26.1 as the only athlete to break 10 minutes and captured the French Throwdown title, arriving as a podium contender and the strongest woman in Europe.

women.name: Aimee Cringle
women.storyline: The trailblazing CrossFitter from the Isle of Man broke into the top 10 with an 8th-place finish at the 2025 Games, a major leap from her 13th-place debut in 2024. After finishing runner-up to Mirjam von Rohr at the 2026 French Throwdown, the former student nurse turned full-time athlete is firmly in the conversation as Britain's best shot at the women's podium.

women.name: Ella Wilkinson
women.storyline: A former gymnast and trampolinist who once trained weekly with 2013 champ Sam Briggs, the UK's Wilkinson finally broke through after years of near-misses, taking 3rd at the 2026 MAD Fitness Festival to earn her first-ever Games berth. The Adidas-backed rookie opened that semifinal with an event win and is a feel-good story to track in San Jose.

women.name: Paige Rodgers
women.storyline: Won the 2026 Mayhem Classic outright roughly seven months postpartum, a remarkable comeback after stepping away to have her daughter. A Mayhem-trained, teen-division veteran who finished 10th at the 2023 Games, she is back among the elite and the first 2026 women's qualifier off the board.

women.name: Siria Meha
women.storyline: The first Albanian athlete ever to reach the CrossFit Games, Meha (born and raised in Italy until age 15) returns for her second straight appearance after a 26th-place rookie showing in 2025. She dominated the 2026 Far East Throwdown in Busan, winning four of six events to claim the lone women's Games ticket, cementing her rise from unknown to genuine threat.

women.name: Lydia Fish
women.storyline: The Wisconsin small-town product is on a sharp upward trajectory: after a 13th-place Games debut in 2025, she dominated the 2026 Syndicate Crown semifinal, winning by nearly 100 points and finishing no worse than 6th in any event. Her semifinal-best performance marks her as a potential top-10 (or higher) sophomore breakout.

women.name: Danielle Brandon
women.storyline: One of the sport's most magnetic and resilient veterans, Brandon backed up her career-best 4th-place Games finish in 2025 by grabbing the third and final qualifying spot at the 2026 Syndicate Crown with a clutch final-event surge. A seven-time Games athlete with a track-and-field and gymnastics background, she remains a high-ceiling, high-personality threat.

women.name: Miley Wade
women.storyline: A teenage phenom out of CrossFit Mayhem who won the Girls 16-17 division at the 2025 Teenage CrossFit Games, Wade is making the jump straight to the individual elite ranks in her first-ever Games. After winning the 2026 MODE Classic Elite division and finishing 2nd at the Copa Sur Semifinal, she is one of the youngest and most hyped rookies in the women's field.

women.name: Anikha Greer
women.storyline: After eight years of near-misses, the Prince Edward Island native finally reached the Games in 2025 and promptly finished 9th as a rookie. She dominated the 2026 Copa Sur Semifinal, winning four of six events to take the title by 60-plus points, confirming her arrival as a top-tier individual.

women.name: Gabriela Migala
women.storyline: Poland's perennial threat won the 2026 MAD Fitness Festival outright to punch her ticket, building on her breakout runner-up finish at the 2024 Games. After her best-ever podium, the 'All Gas No Brakes' veteran arrives in San Jose as a legitimate title contender and the most decorated qualifier from the European pipeline.

women.name: Abigail Domit
women.storyline: A steadily improving three-time Games veteran who climbed from 26th (2023) to 15th (2024) to 12th (2025), Domit secured her 2026 return with a 2nd-place finish at the Legends Championship after narrowly missing out at the Mayhem Classic. A former cheerleader and model, she keeps inching toward the sport's top tier.

women.name: Lucy McGonigle
women.storyline: The 18-year-old phenom from Northern Ireland, a two-time teen world champion, stunned the field with an 11th-place finish as a 2025 Games rookie and trains daily against Tia-Clair Toomey-Orr at PRVN. After taking 2nd at the 2026 MAD Fitness Festival, she is the most-hyped young riser to watch for a top-10 leap in her sophomore Games.

women.name: Olivia Kerstetter
women.storyline: The 2023 Rookie of the Year and two-time teen champion stunned the field with a 3rd-place finish at the 2025 Games in just her second individual appearance. After a rocky start to 2026 (53rd in the Open), she rebounded to win the Legends Championship and is the youngest contender expected to challenge the podium.

women.name: Elisa Fuliano
women.storyline: Italy's CrossFit pioneer, Fuliano is the first and only Italian woman to compete individually at the Games, doing so in 2022, 2023 (a national-best 20th) and 2024. After missing 2025, the gymnast-turned-CrossFitter known as 'Fulix' booked her return with a 3rd-place finish at the 2026 French Throwdown, carrying the hopes of the Italian community back to San Jose.

women.name: Alex Gazan
women.storyline: The Las Vegas-based 2023 Games breakout (5th, Most Improved) fought back from a 2024-25 stretch derailed by a car-accident leg fracture that cost her the 2025 Games. She completed the comeback by winning the 2026 Northern California Classic Semifinal with 588 points, never finishing outside the top 10 across seven events.

women.name: Rachel Noel
women.storyline: A Utah-based CrossFit L2 coach at CrossFit 801, Noel reached the 2025 individual Semifinal and broke through in 2026 by finishing 2nd at the Northern California Classic, winning four of seven events to edge in by 10 points. She earns her maiden Games berth as a rookie.

women.name: Hannah Black
women.storyline: An Austin-based coach with degrees in kinesiology and biomechanics, Black reached the 2024 Games on team CrossFit Invictus Unconquerable (8th place) but had never qualified as an individual until now. She won the 2026 REBEL Renegade Games Semifinal in dominant fashion with seven podium finishes across 11 tests, earning her first individual Games ticket as an emotional, decade-in-the-making breakthrough.

women.name: Ellie Turner
women.storyline: A long-touted Australian phenom whose career stalled after a 2024 region-exemption denial and a run of injuries, Turner roared back to finish 2nd at the 2026 Torian Pro and reach her first Games since 2023. Competing in her home Oceania region (and partner to Justin Medeiros), her comeback narrative makes her one of the more compelling women to track.

women.name: Emma Lawson
women.storyline: After sitting out the entire 2025 season with a back injury, Lawson returned and took 2nd at the 2026 Mayhem Classic to punch her Games ticket. The youngest woman ever to podium at the Games (2nd in 2023 at age 18), she is healthy again and chasing the top step she has long been tipped for.

women.name: Haley Adams
women.storyline: The 2018 Fittest Teen on Earth and perennial Games veteran continues her comeback arc after stepping away in 2023 for her mental health, finishing 2nd at the 2026 Syndicate Crown to lock in another trip. With a career-best 4th (2020) and a freshly rediscovered joy for competing, the 'comeback kid' is a fan favorite chasing a return to the podium.

women.name: Kyra Milligan
women.storyline: The breakout story of the 2026 season so far: Milligan won the worldwide Quarterfinals outright, with all four workouts in the global top 25 and the fastest time on the deadlift-and-double-under test. A registered dental hygienist who trains at PRVN, she backed up the QF win with 3rd at the Torian Pro and arrives looking to shatter her 22nd-place individual debut from 2024.

women.name: Madeline Sturt
women.storyline: After a four-year drought from the Games (2020-2023) where she 'stopped believing' in herself, Sturt completed a remarkable resurgence with an 8th in 2024 and a career-best 6th in 2025, and she won the 2026 Torian Pro to enter as a genuine podium threat. A core member of the dominant PRVN squad alongside partner Jay Crouch, she is one of the most experienced and in-form women in the field.

women.name: Alexis Raptis
women.storyline: A four-time individual Games veteran with back-to-back 6th-place finishes in 2023 and 2024, Raptis came to CrossFit from gymnastics and trains out of Novi CrossFit in Michigan. She won the 2026 online Individual Semifinal outright as the top qualifier of the cohort.

women.name: Erica Folo
women.storyline: A Burlington, Ontario native who started CrossFit at 14 at CrossFit Connection after a background in sprinting, Folo is a fast-rising prospect tipped as a future face of the sport. She finished 2nd in the 2026 online Individual Semifinal to secure her first individual Games berth as a rookie.

women.name: Matilde Garnes
women.storyline: Norway's Matilde Garnes trains at CrossFit Oslo Kriger and is a multiple-time iF3 functional fitness world champion with two prior individual Games trips (19th in 2022). She finished 4th in the 2026 online Individual Semifinal and claimed the final automatic qualifying spot once Alex Gazan's place was reassigned, Gazan having already qualified via the NorCal Classic.

women.name: Jess Green
women.storyline: Australia's Jess Green represents CrossFit Chocolate Box on Sydney's Northern Beaches and built momentum through 2026, placing 3rd in Oceania at Quarterfinals. She finished tied for 5th in the online Individual Semifinal to earn her first individual Games appearance as a rookie.

women.name: Arielle Loewen
women.storyline: A Midland, Texas native who self-coaches from her garage gym, Loewen is one of the sport's most consistent veterans, with a 2023 Games podium (3rd) and a 5th-place finish in 2025. After skipping the in-person Semifinals, she went all-in on the 2026 online Individual Semifinal and qualified, finishing tied for 5th.

women.name: Claudia Gluck
women.storyline: France's top female CrossFitter, Gluck trains in Alsace and broke through with a 12th-place Games rookie season in 2024 followed by 14th in 2025. She was sharp all 2026, taking 7th in the worldwide Open, then locked her third straight Games trip by finishing tied for 5th in the online Individual Semifinal.

women.name: Janie Cheverie
women.storyline: A 23-year-old Canadian rookie from the North America West region, Cheverie trains at home under Brute Strength coaching and earned her first Games berth through the 2026 online Individual Semifinal. She placed 8th but claimed the final qualifying spot after Alex Gazan, who finished higher, had already qualified via the NorCal Classic.
